fighterA.name: Character A

dossier.style: Masterful synthesis of Jeet Kune Do. Bruce Lee combines boxing, fencing, and Wing Chun into one fluid system, eliminating unnecessary movements in favor of direct interception of the enemy's attack.
dossier.advantage: Extremely trained body and inhuman speed. Possesses total muscle control, allowing him to deliver powerful strikes from zero distance.
dossier.mentality: Instant adaptation and instinctive precision. Reads the opponent's intentions in a fraction of a second, striking where the defense is weakest, without sticking to rigid patterns.

powers: Elite human speed, reflexes, coordination, and precision striking.
tools: JKD interception timing, low kicks, rhythm disruption, and cross-style adaptation.
weaknesses: Significant size and reach deficit versus heavyweight specialists.

crucialFeats: Built Jeet Kune Do by effectively combining multiple styles.

fighterB.name: Character B

dossier.style: Masterful control of distance and rhythm. Uses legendary footwork and a fast jab to frustrate enemies and score points from a safe distance.
dossier.advantage: Heavyweight endurance and ring intelligence. Can take a punch, but his true strength lies in avoiding them and dictating the pace of the fight.
dossier.mentality: Charismatic showman with a will of steel. Provokes the opponent to throw them off balance and methodically break their self-confidence.
dossier.quote: Float like a butterfly, sting like a bee.

powers: Elite heavyweight boxing speed, timing, durability, and ring IQ.
tools: Jab control, footwork, defensive movement, clinch management, and pacing control.
weaknesses: Primarily boxing-centric toolkit compared with broad open-rule combat sets.

crucialFeats: Defeated 21 champions or heavyweight title challengers.

tactical-board.headline: TACTICAL BOARD // BRUCE VS ALI
tactical-board.subtitle: Artist versus Boxer
tactical-board.lane: Bruce wins by keeping the fight unstable. Ali wins by making every exchange look like heavyweight reality.

parameter-comparison.headline: PARAMETER COMPARISON
parameter-comparison.subtitle: Average stat profile map
parameter-comparison.left_notes: Entry speed, rhythm disruption, and angle changes
parameter-comparison.right_notes: Reach, durability, pacing, and repeatable ring control
parameter-comparison.draw_notes: Both read timing well, but Ali turns repeated exchanges into his fight

battle-dynamics.headline: BATTLE DYNAMICS
battle-dynamics.subtitle: How the fight changes minute by minute.
battle-dynamics.notes: Bruce is live early because speed and disruption matter most before the fight settles. Ali grows stronger as range, pacing, and durability compound over repeated exchanges.

interpretation.headline: INTERPRETATION
interpretation.subtitle: Who wins the fight on paper?
interpretation.body: Muhammad Ali. Bruce owns speed, disruption, and the uglier opening texture, but Ali owns the categories that settle repeated human exchanges: reach, durability, pacing, and ring management. Bruce only narrows the matchup if he prevents the fight from hardening into Ali's preferred distance game.

fight-simulation.headline: FIGHT SIMULATION
fight-simulation.subtitle: The course of the fight across three phases.
fight-simulation.phase_1_desc: Bruce attacks rhythm with fast entries and low-line disruption before Ali can settle the ring geography.
fight-simulation.phase_2_desc: Ali taxes distance with the jab, feet, and ring control, forcing Bruce to pay for every re-entry.
fight-simulation.phase_3_desc: The fight either stays ugly and narrow for Bruce or settles into repeatable heavyweight distance, where Ali's durability and pace take over.

stat-trap.headline: STAT TRAP
stat-trap.subtitle: Why better stats do not guarantee victory
stat-trap.question: Can Bruce stop the fight from turning into Ali's range-and-tax pattern?
stat-trap.body: Bruce's best edges change the texture of the fight more than the winner identity. Speed and style can win moments, but Ali's proof under sustained heavyweight pressure is the real separator.

final-summary.headline: FINAL SUMMARY
final-summary.subtitle: Summary
final-summary.line_1: Ali owns the paper comparison, 87.67 vs 78.89.
final-summary.line_2: Bruce changes the texture of the fight more than the winner identity.
final-summary.line_3: Open rules narrow the matchup, but do not flip the baseline result.
